The Courage to Question Our Own Certainty

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (740 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • In a recent development, there are a plethora of potentially polarizing problems these days in all aspects of our lives!
  • According to recent reports, our positioning and decisions on an issue seem like they happen in the blink of an eye.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

In a recent development, there are a plethora of potentially polarizing problems these days in all aspects of our lives! It seems that we can hardly get a point of view on the table before a fellow conversationalist debunks our idea and discredits us along the way. Take your pick from a bushel full of igniting issues, whether it be global warming, wars, increasing the tax percentage for the very wealthy, or the strengths and weaknesses of our favorite political personalities; there will be no shortage of strong opinions. You can also be assured that before the full set of points of view are exposed or explored, one or more folks will have already decided what the correct point of view should be.

According to recent reports, our positioning and decisions on an issue seem like they happen in the blink of an eye. This instant judgement can create ill will, stress for us and the other, and can challenge or ruin long-standing relationships. Furthermore, it will likely lead to a suboptimal exploration and resolution of the salient points of view. The pivot that I would like to explore is realizing that although our interpretations and positions usually feel quite certain to us, they most likely do not represent the whole of the reality of that situation; they are a narrower, biased slice of the problem or solution.

It has been revealed that I would like to explore what can happen when we can loosen our grip on our story/point of view, and instead consider what might ensue if we instead question our own certainty. This, of course, would require slowing down enough to really listen first and then explore the fuller reality of the situation together; then, with skillful listening and openness to other ways of thinking, we can have a meaningful and civil dialogue.

In a recent development, we seem to be experiencing a plethora of fractured conversations, competing accounts of the truth, information overload, and fear about the future, all of which are leading to what we might call “contemporary exhaustion.” And if the impact of this on us personally wasn’t enough, the relational tension as well as the societal and political challenges are at an all-time high. It is so much more likely that answers to our difficult questions will land somewhere in the middle of the two opposing extremes being debated, or in a yet-to-be-discovered “third alternative” idea that cannot possibly be uncovered because of the anger, tension, and lack of listening in the interchange. Just to ground this idea in one statistic: the American Psychological Association's Stress in America survey, "A Crisis of Connection," reported that 62% of adults considered societal divisions a significant stressor in their lives.

If you are willing to have the “courage to suspend the certainty” of your initial interpretation and allow for more information, thoughts, and feelings to emerge between you and another, amazing things can happen. Try following a simple practice of what I will call “thoughtful receptivity” using these 4 steps. Imagine that, before you know it, you are in a polarizing conversation with challenging points of view and heated feelings emerging. Each side draws his/her sword, and the point-counterpoint debate begins. You have enough presence to realize you are in the battle, and it likely will not end well. You feel triggered and notice the same for the other person. You remember this practice and do the following:.

In a recent development, we all have the tendency to confuse the story we have crafted and are trying to tell with the whole truth about a situation. Perhaps a better way to proceed is to remain open to what we have not yet explored or understood, remain open to another way of thinking about a situation, and remain open to the other person. If we could find the grace to do so, we might learn to see and understand more deeply before we judge. All of this ultimately requires that we develop the courage to question our own certainty. If we could do so, it is very likely that our world would become a much better, kinder place to live and thrive.

American Psychological Association. (2025). Stress in America 2025: A crisis of connection. https://www.apa.org/pubs/reports/stress-in-america/2025.

A rare triple-star system near Earth ‘should not exist’

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, “The system should not exist,” Patrick Dufour, a University of Montreal astrophysicist and study co-author, noted in a statement.
  • It has been revealed that dufour’s team first noticed the perplexing triple-star system while scanning for exoplanets using highly sensitive equipment mounted on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope near the dormant volcano of Mauna Kea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, astronomers searching for new exoplanets recently found something much stranger—a rarely seen triple-star system located only 28 light-years away from Earth. If that weren’t odd enough, two of its three stellar components are dense, depleted white dwarfs. A study recently published in the Astronomy & Astrophysics Journal details an oddball trio that is so perplexing that researchers still aren’t quite sure how it formed in the first place.

According to recent reports, “The system should not exist,” Patrick Dufour, a University of Montreal astrophysicist and study co-author, noted in a statement. “We have no clean explanation for how it got here.”.

It has been revealed that dufour’s team first noticed the perplexing triple-star system while scanning for exoplanets using highly sensitive equipment mounted on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope near the dormant volcano of Mauna Kea. Astronomers were specifically looking for subtle discrepancies in the movements of distant stars, which often indicates that there are orbiting planets nearby.

But when it came to one particular red dwarf, the data simply didn’t make sense. Rather than delicate shifts in motion, researchers recorded velocity swings at speeds nearing 10 miles per second. This effect was too much for a single planet to cause, and after years of additional observations, astronomers determined that whatever the unseen subject was, it possessed a mass greater than half the sun.

“The object’s unusual combination of high mass and dim light left only one plausible explanation: it was the remains of a dead star,” explained Charles-Antoine Parent, a University of Montreal astronomer and study co-author.

Possible suspects included a neutron star and even a secret black hole, but some assistance from the Gemini North telescope also on Mauna Kea finally confirmed its identity: a close-orbiting white dwarf. This complicated the situation. Astronomers previously discovered another white dwarf circling the red dwarf at a much greater distance. Taken altogether, that made three stars existing in a single system. The grouping is now known as Welopō‘ai, a Hawaiian phrase that roughly translates to “path of family traits” in reference to the stars’ shared relationships. According to researchers, no other comparable example can be found within 100 light-years of Earth.

According to recent reports, however, Welopō‘ai still doesn’t quite add up. The red dwarf’s nearest companion was about 40 percent more massive than our sun prior to transforming into a white dwarf. When it did, it would have expanded hundreds of times its original size. Previously documented systems featuring these dynamics entailed the two stars falling into an even tighter orbit, or even merging. Despite this, Welopō‘ai’s red dwarf is still there and in a strikingly stable, wide orbit with the closest white dwarf. The team now plans to continue observing their discovery to learn as much as possible about the triple-star system, and possibly figure out how it formed in the first place.

“Discoveries like this remind us that our own cosmic neighborhood still contains remarkable surprises,” added study co-author and astronomer, Étienne Artigau.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Meet the experts: Diana Pearre, MD, gynecologic oncologist at The Roy and Patricia Disney Family Cancer Center at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, CA; Abdulrahman Sinno, MD, chief of the division of gynecologic oncology with Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, part of the University of Miami Health System.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 21,000 women in the U.S. are diagnosed with ovarian cancer each year. While it’s not the most common cancer in women, ovarian cancer is considered the deadliest cancer in women worldwide because it’s often diagnosed at later stages, has a high rate of recurrence, and is difficult to treat. Right now, the five-year survival rate of ovarian cancer is just 52 percent.

As with most cancers, detecting the disease early may increase the odds of survival. Researchers recently discovered a latest way to detect earlier stages of the cancer, potentially helping thousands of women. The Nature Medicine study breaks down the mechanisms of a blood-based test that can detect ovarian cancer in its precancerous stages. In theory, this could dramatically impact survival rates in women. The test is still in the research phases, but doctors agree that something like this is needed. Here’s what they want women to know.

Meet the experts: Diana Pearre, MD, gynecologic oncologist at The Roy and Patricia Disney Family Cancer Center at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, CA; Abdulrahman Sinno, MD, chief of the division of gynecologic oncology with Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, part of the University of Miami Health System.

First, some background: Researchers found that women with early-stage high-grade serous ovarian cancer or serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC), which is a precursor to ovarian cancer, have higher-than-usual levels of a type of RNA called Tu-stroma circulating in their blood.

According to recent reports, tu-Stroma is linked with cancer’s early attacks that weaken healthy cells to make room for cancer cell growth. Spotting Tu-stroma means that doctors have an early molecular warning signal that could suggest cancer is developing before a tumor is detected.

In a recent development, the study itself was conducted on hundreds of women around the world with and without cancer and found that the test detected STIC in 92.3 percent of women with the condition. It also correctly identified 98.2 percent of healthy women. They also tried the test on a high-risk group and found that about 72 percent of positive results were accurate, while negative results were almost 100 percent accurate.

But this is still an early discovery, and the researchers point out in the study that more robust research is needed.

In a recent development, “We have very few ways of detecting ovarian cancer,” states Diana Pearre, MD, gynecologic oncologist at The Roy and Patricia Disney Family Cancer Center at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, California. “There are no screening tests.” Instead, doctors rely on pelvic ultrasounds and labs to look for tumor markers.

Industry observers note that “Unfortunately, we subject women to surgery if and when they have ovarian masses that are suspicious,” Dr. Pearre says. “Having another tool to help us discriminate which tumors are more suspicious would be very helpful in detecting cancers at an early stage.”.

In a recent development, abdulrahman Sinno, MD, chief of the division of gynecologic oncology with Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, part of the University of Miami Health System, agrees. “Eighty percent of high-grade serous carcinoma is diagnosed in advanced stage with no effective screening strategy,” he notes.

Previous screening strategies didn’t work because they only spotted cancer at advanced stages, Dr. Sinno notes. “Before this, there was no screening test for average-risk women,” he adds.

We’re not at the stage where this can be rolled out to the general public yet. The blood test is still considered experimental and it’s not a clinically validated. Still, doctors say the news is worth following. “This is a promising discovery-stage result, not a test that is ready for prime time,” Dr. Sinno claims.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Social media influencers claim that having a “ferritin face” may indicate you’re low in iron.
  • Ferritin is a protein that helps your body store iron.
  • As “ferritin face” makes its way across social media platforms, consumers are describing several tell-tale signs, including:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Social media influencers claim that having a “ferritin face” may indicate you’re low in iron.

Ferritin is a protein that helps your body store iron. You need iron in order to make healthy red blood cells, which carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body. Iron is also notable for bone marrow, organs, healthy muscles, and brain development.

As “ferritin face” makes its way across social media platforms, consumers are describing several tell-tale signs, including:.

Sources indicate that users have also shared images of their face before and after taking iron supplements or getting an iron infusion. Videos about “ferritin face” have garnered millions of views on various platforms.

However, medical professionals state that your appearance alone is not enough to diagnose iron deficiency.

“It’s notable to understand that ferritin face is not a medical diagnosis, nor is it a confirmed symptom of iron deficiency. While some people with iron deficiency can appear pale due to low hemoglobin levels in their red blood cells, there are many other symptoms to consider,” said Daniel Atkinson, a general practitioner in the United Kingdom and clinical lead at Treated.

“Notably, these symptoms are also present in many different conditions, and their presence does not necessarily mean iron deficiency anemia or even low ferritin levels. Similar features are seen in people with iron processing and absorption issues, such as gluten intolerance, or in urgent sudden blood loss scenarios,” added Jonathan Jennings, MD, board certified internist at Medical Offices of Manhattan.

Iron deficiency can affect your skin and appearance. These signs are often subtle, but may include:.

In some ways, the social media videos are correct. Your skin and face can change when your iron levels are low.

According to recent reports, “The facial signs people point to, like pale skin and a washed-out look, mostly come from anaemia, when your haemoglobin has dropped. But iron deficiency and anaemia aren’t the same thing,” stated Thom Phillips, a general practitioner in the United Kingdom and Chief Medical Officer at Forth. “By the time low iron indicates on your face, your stores are usually close to empty.”.

It is important to speak with a healthcare professional, who will run blood tests such as a complete blood count and ferritin levels.

It is also key not to take iron supplements without first checking with your healthcare professional, because having too much iron in your body can also cause negative effects.

Too little and too much iron could raise your risk of infection, which is why it’s important not to take supplements without medical supervision.

The signs and symptoms of iron deficiency can depend on whether you are anemic or not. Some of the early signs may include:.

“These symptoms typically occur because your body produces fewer red blood cells, which results in less oxygen being delivered throughout your body, making you feel tired and weak,” mentioned Atkinson.

Less common symptoms may include:.

While your facial appearance can be a sign that something isn’t right, healthcare professionals consider other symptoms and how you feel overall.

They also rely on blood tests to confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment.

Sources indicate that “The misinformation is the idea that you can spot it yourself. That leads to two problems: people with low iron who look fine assume they’re OK, and people who look tired start taking iron supplements they don’t need,” mentioned Phillips.

Atkinson also noted that factors such as different settings and environmental conditions can affect how your face appears.

That being said, the “ferritin face” trend may help bring awareness to certain symptoms and when to get them checked.

“[This] trend may raise some awareness about iron deficiency anemia and how low iron levels can impact daily life,” stated Atkinson.

“Fatigue and lightheadedness are common side effects of low iron, but it manifests in other ways too, such as paler skin or increased hair shedding, which can be concerning for many people. If you experience these symptoms, you should let your doctor know so they can help treat the condition appropriately,” he stated.

  • Industry observers note that despite the growing recall population, the core issue remains generally unchanged from previous Takata recalls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

18 years after Honda filed the first official airbag recall and 12 years since the first round of mass recalls began, the Takata airbag scandal remains ongoing. This month, Honda and Toyota have both filed latest recalls with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration related to faulty airbag inflators.

The pair of recalls filed in November include a population of more than 1.6 million vehicles. Late-model Hondas make up over 810,000 units in the recall, while Toyota accounts for 790,000 units, 314,000 of which are located in the United States. NHTSA documents indicate that 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX, 2013 Acura RDX models, 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 ‌IS250, ⁠2017 GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia and 2016-2017 4Runner models are included in the recall.

Industry observers note that despite the growing recall population, the core issue remains generally unchanged from previous Takata recalls. “The airbag inflator propellant can degrade with repeated exposure to high-humidity environments and large temperature variation, resulting in increased internal pressure. If an affected airbag deploys, the increased internal pressure may cause the inflator to rupture (break apart) and deploy abnormally,” NHTSA documents explain. “In the event of an inflator rupture, metal fragments could pass through the airbag cushion material possibly causing serious injury or fatality to vehicle occupants.”.

There have been no injuries or crashes tied to the vehicles being newly recalled. However, NHTSA has recorded 28 deaths in the United States and more than 400 injuries stemming from defective Takata airbag inflators since 2009. The Takata airbag recall remains the largest recall in U.S. history.

Given the rolling nature of the Takata recall, Honda and Toyota were already in discussions with federal regulators when this airbag version began to show signs of degradation. Honda first identified an matter during simulation testing under severe environmental conditions in May 2025. However, these tests didn’t show abnormal inflator behavior or a “statistically significant deviation” from previous prediction models. Similarly, Toyota had been collecting and studying certain Takata inflators since 2016, specifically focusing on a desiccated, phase-stabilized ammonium nitrate (PSAN) propellant. Toyota’s predictive models indicated that some of these inflators could be reaching the end of their life, prompting the Japanese automaker to conduct a voluntary safety recall.

It has been revealed that the remedy is fairly simple for both automakers: Toyota and Honda will simply replace the airbag inflators on affected units. Honda indicates its newly introduced inflators are manufactured by a different supplier and use a different propellant that does not degrade over the long term when exposed to high temperatures, high humidity, and large temperature fluctuations. Either way, both automakers and federal regulators urge affected owners to have their airbag inflators swapped out as soon as possible.

A Fresh York transplant hailing from the Pacific Northwest, Emmet White has a passion for anything that goes: cars, bicycles, planes, and motorcycles. After learning to ride at 17, Emmet worked in the motorcycle industry before joining Autoweek in 2022 and Road & Track in 2024. The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

30+ editor-approved practical gifts for 2026

Industry observers note that we may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn more ›.

It has been revealed that in my eyes, the best gift is a practical one. It’s useful and won’t rot in the back of someone’s closet for years; they’ll think of you whenever they use it; and you get major brownie points for introducing a magical, miracle product into their life. And what’s better than being known as someone who reliably gifts reliable products? I may still get made fun of by family for my history of wanting practical gifts (including lead refills for my mechanical pencil), but the gifts I treasure most often get the most use in my home. If you know someone automating their smart home, we’ve got a separate guide for that. But if you’re looking for purpose-driven products, below you’ll find some of the best practical gear to give to friends and family members who value utilitarianism over flash and fluff.

The OLIGHT Baton4 Pro rechargeable flashlight is a $63 flashlight that’s well worth the cost. They’ll never need another flashlight, and they’ll struggle to find one as bright and powerful as this. This torch clocks in at 1600 lumens, and its beam reaches 200 meters long, with a cool white color that cuts through the darkest sky. Dual switches—a side switch and tail switch—allow for one-handed mode selection (choose from high, turbo, and momentary on). Use it hands-free with an included L stand that sticks to metal surfaces, and know it will stay cool and comfortable in hand, even in Turbo mode. Charge it with the included magnetic charger, or unscrew the tailcap to reveal a USB-C port for universal charging anywhere. Your next power outage, camping trip, and attic exploration mission will thank you for this gift.

It has been revealed that carry an entire box’s worth of tools in your hand with this $130 LEATHERMAN Wave Plus 18-in-1 Multi-Tool. Standouts and crowd-pleasers include regular pliers, needle-nose pliers, replaceable wire cutters, knives, a saw, a can opener, a bottle opener, spring-action scissors, and three driver sizes. This multitool is made to be portable, reliable, durable, and multifunctional, all ingredients for one practical gift.

Made from 100 percent Greek Koroneiki olives, this single-varietal, cold-extracted, early harvest extra virgin olive oil adds zest to whatever you love best. From a bowl of simple greens to artisan bread, grilled fish to wood-fired vegetables, you’ll love the grassy, sassy brightness it brings. And that’s how you also know it’s packed with plenty of polyphenols, so you can fight free radicals—reducing inflammation while elevating taste. Combine it with basil and black olives for the kind of flavor the foodies in your life will want to put on a pedestal (not included) … just one of the many kitchen gifts we can recommend.

Industry observers note that being backstage at a show is a vibe. Sometimes weird, sometimes wild, but always an interesting mix of calm and chaos. Chicago’s FRET12 brand aims to capture the smell of decompression and anticipation and bring it home with its hand-poured “Green Room” candle, which blends birch, bark, fig, and bergamot into something restful and ripe you can gift the joint audiophile-aromaphile in your orbit. For something more after-hours and intimate, try “Deep Cuts,” or spark up “Campfire Acoustic” and bask in wafts of sweet, warm smoke and vanilla. Available in 3-, 8-, and 10-ounce sizes. And while you’re at it, pick up a custom-designed and -printed T-shirt and other garb for that special member of your personal road crew who wants to celebrate their love of all things analog while they shop for some M&M’s (no brown ones) and white tube socks. And there’s artwork and actual guitar stuff, too, for gigging musicians!

Recent findings suggest that the Mileseey GeneSonic Pro and GenePro G1 give you what you want for a casual round with friends, and what you need if you still want to know that carry number or feel confident before you even swing a club in more serious competition. The IP65 GenePro G1 delivers accuracy on par with top-of-the-line rangefinders on the market today, while also giving you a full view of the hole. It offers front/center/back yardages, Ball-to-Pin distance, 600-yard flag-lock, SmartSlope compensation, and more. And the IP67 magnetically mounted GeneSonic Pro speaker delivers quality sound and a built-in detachable GPS with 43,000+ preloaded advanced course views for those pesky cart path-only days. Plus, it’s a 30W power bank, so you can get out and continue to jam out, no matter what the weather brings or how you swing. Whichever one suits your game, you can’t go wrong, and they make a great gift for the golfer in your life.

If you’re looking to give a gift that no one asks for but nearly everybody needs, four upcoming tires is something someone you know has been putting off. If you know someone with a pickup, SUV, or van that is constantly on the road in mixed conditions, including snow, you can show you care about their safety with four Kumho Road Venture HT tires [left, above]. They come with a 75,000-mile tread warranty on passenger sizes (50,000 on LT sizes), so this is something they won’t have to think about again for years. The zig-zag tread and 3D interlocking sipes earn these a Three-Peak Mountain Snowflake, which means they beat a standard tire’s acceleration on medium-packed snow by at least 10 percent. Meanwhile, four deep grooves channel water away when rain is the bigger problem, and staggered tread blocks mean less highway hum in general. If you know a driver going everywhere (except off-road), you’ll be giving them smoother rides on a road trip, fewer white-knuckle mornings (even in January), and no tire talk for a while. Having taken them out on a closed course near Seattle, we can confirm good dry grip, even during aggressive cornering, and well-composed wet performance. No, they might not unwrap these and squeal … but with fresh tread, these tires shouldn’t squeal either, and that’s something to get excited about. If the person you’re gifting is an SUV or crossover driver more interested in a quiet, plush ride over snow grip, the Crugen GT Pro [right, above], packed with resonance-reduction tech, offers less wheel slip under hard acceleration, strong hydroplaning resistance, and consistent cabin quietness compared to whatever bald rubber they’ve been riding on for too long.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve sung the praises of this $98 Levoit Core300-P air purifier for years. It’s one of our best budget air purifiers, and there are currently two of them in my home: one in the primary bedroom and another in the living room. The replaceable filters aren’t prohibitively expensive, and they’re whisper-quiet at their lowest speeds. I’ve tested many air purifiers, and this one easily beats its more expensive competitors. My asthmatic cat loves this air purifier, my fiancé, who hasn’t gotten sick in years, loves it, and I love it. I’d buy it for all my friends if I could.

Good things come in small packages, including this $180 Midea dehumidifier, which is two feet high and a little over a foot wide. This small dehumidifier holds 3.2 gallons of water and can cover 1,500 square feet, making it perfect for apartments, bathrooms, and even damp walk-in closets. Control it via app or voice, or use the built-in buttons. A side window reveals when it’s time to empty the water tank, and a handle makes it easy to carry. The dehumidifier is also on wheels, so you don’t even have to carry it in some cases.

In a recent development, other humidifiers promptly get gross and grody. The Carepod One is a splurge at $279, but this high-end humidifier stays mold-free thanks to a sterilizable, dishwasher-safe stainless steel basin. It has only three parts to clean: the white wand, stainless steel water tank, and stainless steel inner lid. The humidifier runs for up to 30 hours and includes a built-in timer for hassle-free use. It’s Restriction of Hazardous Substances-certified, meaning it’s free of hazardous substances like lead and mercury.

In a recent development, sometimes, a mess isn’t messy enough to warrant breaking out the significant, heavy vacuum, and there is no other pleasure like having a tool for a very specific task. This $80 handheld vacuum from Shark is excellent for cleaning pet hair off couches or collecting the crust from your car. An extra-large dust cup means you can clean all these small messes in one go or have extra room for pet hair when the couch gets particularly fuzzy.

Regardless of water bottle allegiance, the $20 Kuppy Silicone Water Bottle Drying Rack helps reusable bottles of all sizes, wine glasses, and even silicone snack bags dry thoroughly to prevent odor from trapped water. They’re stackable for storage in the water bottle section of a kitchen (Everyone has a Water Bottle Kingdom somewhere in their home). Best of all, they take up less space than traditional dish racks.

Sources indicate that this $37 Aquabliss SF100 Daily Revitalize Shower Filter is for the person in your life who has a codependent relationship with their Brita pitcher. This budget shower filter fits standard fittings and works with fixed, rain, handheld, and combination shower heads. It also adds three to four inches to an existing shower arm and maintains water pressure for cleaner water without weaker streams. The filter cartridge takes two minutes to replace and lasts three to six months depending on water quality.

The Philips Sonicare Prestige 9900 is a $380 rechargeable toothbrush that provides dentist-level cleaning every day. Sonic technology and multi-angle bristles remove plaque regardless of brush technique. SenseIQ Technology automatically adjusts intensity and flashes when it detects too much pressure. This toothbrush comes with five modes, plus three intensity levels. The Oral-B iO Series 3 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush is a cheaper option that’s still just as giftable.

In a recent development, A water flosser is the bedrock of a well-rounded oral care routine. The Waterpik Aquarius Countertop Water Flosser is a $100 countertop water flosser that’s more like a power washer for mouths. Choose from 10 settings for extra pearly whites, including a massage mode that helps stimulate gums. Although it’s not a replacement for floss, it’s excellent for getting the job done after a late night. I personally use mine after flossing and add a bit of mouthwash to the reservoir to get fluoride where my teeth need it most.

The Nori Press Travel Steam Iron is a $120 handheld iron that resembles a giant hair straightener. If your gift recipient is like me and has ironed out my polo collars with a hair straightener, this iron should feel familiar. Two heated plates iron the front and back of a garment at once, removing wrinkles without an ironing board. The compact iron also includes a built-in steamer to remove wrinkles from more delicate fabrics. At 14 inches long and weighing a little under 1.5 pounds, it’s packable for clothing emergencies.

Recent findings suggest that the Dyson Supersonic Nural Hair Dryer is a $450 hair dryer designed to maintain healthy hair and a healthy scalp. It’s also engineered to reduce flakes and shedding and balance hair oils. This smart hair dryer reduces airflow and deactivates the heater when set down; a Hall sensor recognizes each attachment as it’s used and automatically adjusts settings based on the attachment; and intelligent heat control monitors airflow to prevent hair damage. It also dries hair fast, a plus for practical friends who hate going to bed with wet hair.

It has been revealed that your most practical friend is most likely a Virgo or Capricorn. Popular Science’s resident Virgo and Managing Editor, Gear & Commerce, enjoys using this Baldscaper to keep his head smooth without causing physical/emotional damage to himself and his loved ones. Four floating shaver heads contour to the head, face, and body for a smooth shave, cutting it close sans nicks and razor burn. It’s fully waterproof, rinses clean with just water, and can be used wet or dry. A powerful motor and 90-minute battery life cut through coarse hair without dying halfway through a head shave.

The TUSHY Classic 3.0 Bidet is a $124 starter bidet that helps your gift recipient feel cleaner than using toilet paper alone. It includes all materials needed for installation, which takes less than 10 minutes. A Schmutz Shield (actual name for this feature) blocks grime from escaping past the toilet lid, and a self-cleaning nozzle means this bidet won’t cause more cleaning-related headaches your practical friend may experience daily.

In a recent development, shark makes some of the best cordless vacuums, and this $380 option includes some of our favorite features in a vacuum cleaner, including a MultiFLEX wand that makes it infinitely easier to reach under furniture, a light that reveals missed spots, and Floor Detect technology that adjusts brushroll speed depending on the surface. It also doubles as a handvac and comes with tools for crevices and upholstery. With 50 minutes of runtime, HEPA filtration, and an anti-allergen seal, dust busting won’t involve a sneezing fit.

Industry observers note that give the gift of a fully connected home with the $130 Aeotec Smart Home Hub2, which can be used as a SmartThings Hub and supports Zigbee and Matter Gateway protocols. It’s also compatible with Alexa, Google Assistant, and Wi-Fi. Although it’s not Z-Wave compliant, it offers wider device compatibility and stronger security than some competitors.

It has been revealed that the best electric blankets provide warmth without turning up the thermostat. This $50 electric throw blanket from Westinghouse is reliable and heats evenly. Plus, it protects itself from overheating and includes an auto-off function for peace of mind when a nap strikes. A weighty smart digital controller cycles through six heat settings and a timer up to 10 hours. Throw it in the washing machine and hang it to dry between seasons.

The Rumpl Gametime Puffy is a $100 2-in-1 stadium accessory made for overtime, any time. It packs a full-size 50×70″ insulated blanket into a TPU-laminated storage case featuring an adjustable, removable shoulder strap and an integrated 1-inch insulated foam pad to sit on when you pull the blanket out (and it’s an extra-padded 4” cushion with the blanket in). The shell and case have a PFAS-free water-repellent finish, and the blanket keeps you warm down to 45 degrees, making it great for football games, soccer matches, and club tournaments.

According to recent reports, I’ve assembled my fair share of furniture from a multinational home furnishings store, and let’s be real: Sometimes those Allen wrenches don’t cut it. Enter the Greenworks Pro PowerAll 24V Drill Driver and Impact Driver Combo Kit, a $169 bundle that gives you two handy tools for the price of one. The drill driver and impact driver use brushless motors and 24-volt batteries, and run 20% longer than 18- and 20-volt counterparts. It’s compact, lightweight, and easy to use in tight spaces, making it an excellent gift for DIY-minded friends and family.

Sources indicate that the $65 Anyday 4-Piece Medium Glass Food Storage system is made for microwaving or cooking directly in the oven, thanks to sturdy borosilicate glass that’s stronger and better resists extreme temperature changes than soft glass. The glass dishware is even freezer-safe. A glass lid prevents splatters in the microwave; lay-flat knobs vent food while cooking or create an airtight seal when it’s time to store any leftovers.

This $160 waterproof, compact carry-all from RUX works like an everyday tote, then converts to a roll-top dry bag to protect against rain and random liquids. It fits a laptop, lunch, and any layers, while internal and external pockets keep keys, a phone, and wallet within reach. Grab it by the handles, or wear it crossbody with the included shoulder strap on a two-hands kind of day. Exterior lash points connect pockets and panels (sold separately) for added storage and organization if your gift recipient desires a gift that keeps on giving.

Practical people definitely have plenty of pen opinions—I know I do. And this $6.50 pack of uniball Jetstream pens is a favorite thanks to its smooth, opaque, quick-drying ink that’s water- and fade-resistant. Choose the .7 millimeter option for a finer line, or the 1 millimeter thickness for those who prefer a more robust script.

Industry observers note that my $26 LEUCHTTURM1917 A5 notebook holds my journal ramblings, my to-do lists, and random neurotic notes I need to get out of my head and onto a page. Numbered pages, two page markers, and a blank table of contents help organize all my jumbled thoughts. I personally go for a hardcover notebook with ruled paper, but LEUCHTTURM1917 also sells softcover journals in every color of the rainbow, with square grid ruling, dotted ruling, or blank pages.

Industry observers note that the Ember Mug 3 is the latest generation of the popular smart mug that can keep hot drinks at a precise temperature all day long. Each 14 oz mug includes a sliding lid that extends battery life up to three hours on a single charge (it’s 80 minutes without the lid). And a charging coaster recharges your mug after your daily dose of bean juice (or maintains the temperature indefinitely if you keep the mug on it). Customize your preferred temperature in the app, or set it manually with a button on the mug. It’s also top-rack dishwasher safe.

According to recent reports, this $35 leakproof travel mug from BrüMate is for those who don’t mix their coffee with their electronics. A ceramic lining preserves flavor while preventing staining and leftover odors, and triple insulation keeps drinks hot or cold for hours. It’s cup-holder friendly for caffeinating on the go, and a magnetic, OctaLock lid prevents spills while running errands.

It has been revealed that the Click & Carry Ergonomic Grocery Bag Carrier Handle & Bag Holder is a $14 gizmo that saves trips and reduces hassle when unloading groceries. It’s gentle on joints, reduces hand strain, and its ergonomic design lowers injury risk. The bag carrier has a 100-pound weight capacity but weighs just under three ounces. The friend who always tests the boundaries of bringing everything inside in one trip will thank you.

Socks are a well-liked practical gift, and this $25 two-pack of merino wool, COOLMAX EcoMade polyester, REPREVE recycled polyester + nylon socks from Gordini uses fine-gauge and ultra-lightweight yarns to keep feet dry and supported with Linear Wicking Channels that move away moisture and Quilted AirForms that distribute shock and cushion impact. These OrbitFit anatomically mapped 3D zones create a purpose-knit performance fit that keeps you comfortable at home, on a walk, or while running or hiking. If cotton socks are on the gift list, we’re fans of the HUE Women’s Mini Crew Sock and the Men’s Casual Ribbed Crew Socks, which are breathable and comfortable.

The Garmin Venu 4 is a $550 multisport watch that blends style and function. A bright 1.4-inch AMOLED display clearly reveals health and fitness stats like sleep tracking and time needed for workout recovery, along with on-screen workouts. A smart wake alarm helps with waking up at an optimal time, and a built-in LED flashlight illuminates dark morning walks. This watch supports running and triathlon, strength training, jet lag recovery, and more. Data-obsessed friends and family members will be pleased with all the numbers and stats they can pull from this watch.

This $50 OtterBox Symmetry Series Case has protected my iPhone 13 for years: the only blemish is a dent in the aluminum bumper from when I took it out of its case and immediately dropped it on my concrete porch. I’ve learned my lesson and never forgo a phone case. The OtterBox Symmetry Series Case is sleek without being too flimsy and protects without bulk. It’s on my repurchase list and should be on yours, too, especially if you’re looking at one of the upcoming iPhone 18s.

In a recent development, these newly refreshed noise-canceling headphones from Bose are essential for quiet commutes and tuning out the airport chaos while traveling. Bose makes some of our favorite noise-canceling headphones and earbuds thanks to thoughtful design and helpful tech in each pair. We’re particularly fond of the comfortable pill-shaped earcups, 24-hour battery life, Immersive Audio, QuietControl noise cancellation, and updated ActiveSense Tech to smooth sound spikes in Aware Mode.

Recent findings suggest that this practical gift is also personal. Every pair of these $249 orthotics from Stride is custom-made from a 3D scan of someone’s foot and a gait video with just their smartphone required, no doctor’s visit necessary. Take a short quiz about pain areas, activity levels, goals, and shoe preferences; provide the digital data; and podiatrists in Germany customize the orthotics and print them on durable TPU (personalized for the recipient) before they arrive at your doorstep in just 10 to 15 days. And they go well beyond arch support. It’s hard to convey the initially odd and then promptly invigorating sensation of an insole that considers each unique contour of the ball of your foot, but we guarantee your achiest friend or family member will appreciate a custom gift that addresses a major pain point, literally.

I hate when gloves hinder my range of movement. These $85 bike gloves from Hestra have a flexible but durable outer fabric and stretchy polyester on the palm. Primaloft Gold synthetic insulation, a fleece lining, and a membrane that stops rain and slush without making hands clammy keep your fingers warm. And the Lycra-clad slit makes the glove easy to put on and take off. Even if we don’t ride, these gloves could be our ride or die.

It has been revealed that style and practicality can go hand-in-hand. The Danner Chelsea boot is just that: Proudly assembled in the firm’s Portland, Oregon factory with signature stitchdown construction, it slips on and is made of full-grain leather. The nonconductive (Electrical Hazard Certified) outsole is oil- and slip-resistant and is comfortable and durable even after climbing on ladders or standing on unforgiving surfaces like wood, tile, or concrete. Even better, the boots are Danner Recraftable, meaning they are eligible for part replacements, leather care, and restitching (paid services), so you are investing in someone’s ongoing comfort. If your gift recipient is good with laces, the Bull Run Moc Toe is another top choice for both looks and stability.

It has been revealed that these $249 Nike slides are a collab with recovery company Hyperice, known for its wellness and recovery technology (we’re right now testing the Normatec dynamic air compression massage legs to positive effect). The comfortable slides combine heat, vibration, and responsive cushioning to make every step feel lighter. They’re like giving a pair of heated slippers a friar-like tonsure.

There’s a woman in your life who carries the world on their shoulders. They shouldn’t have to carry back pain, too. Maybe you’ve heard about Taylor Swift’s posture-correcting bra, or maybe you’ve just listened to a busty friend (or your mom) complain that her back feels like a janky Jenga stack of crooked vertebrae. Is this nearly $200 bra worth it? In a word: absolutely. Designed in seven sizes, up to a G cup, this FDA-registered posture corrector looks like a high-necked crop top with extra-wide straps and a mesh front panel. It gently pulls shoulders into alignment and hugs the girls with serious support—fair warning, though: it can be a wrestling match to get it on and off at first. This one’s more for workouts or lounging at home than for a lift-and-separate situation. Still, it can battle desk-job hunch and is a major relief from digging bra straps.

Recent findings suggest that know somebody in your family who indicates “I’m just a little stiff!” while grimacing as they ease down the stairs after pickleball? Then you know someone who would appreciate the gift of some McDavid support. For instance, the $56.99 NRG above wraps polymer springs on each side of the knee for energy return, while taking up to 12.5 percent stress off each knee. And if that someone you know if coming back from something more serious than soreness, there are slip-on neoprene sleeves for stability all the way to braces that add Maximum+ support, for serious rehab, once you go up to the hinged Bio-Logix line. And once someone is back to throwing their body around, they could appreciate the HEX padded sleeves and compression tights. Brand ambassador Kyrie Irving vouches for them after a torn ACL. And since McDavid has gear that is HSA/FSA-eligible, you can treat yourself to fatigue relief, too, if you’ve got some use-it-or-lose-it dollars left at the end of 2026.

Just because you see a jacket that you feel suits you doesn’t always mean it fits you. The same goes for folks on your gift list. But there’s an alternative to something off-the-rack that’s right in the shoulders but maybe tight in the hips. Maybe the sleeves are right, but it only works if you don’t zip it. Or maybe it’s only available in cost-prohibitive heirloom hides. Well, the Jacket Maker will cut a style to the wearer’s own measurements, and every measurement in their guide comes with a how-to video to make sure you get it right. The team also checks numbers against standard sizing and clarifies/suggests alterations if anything stands out. After that, decisions come down to the customer, from the leather and lining to adding embroidery or emblems, and choosing different shades of hardware. Once completed and pictures are approved, which can take 5-7 weeks, it’s shipped worldwide for free, with duties included at checkout. Sure, gifting at Christmas means they’ll be wearing it in spring, but there’s a thrill in the customization and anticipation and finally seeing them actually reach for that favorite jacket every time they head toward the door. It’ll give you and them a warm, fuzzy feeling … literally, with the right liner. (And there are plentiful ready-to-wear styles, too, if that’s more your jam.).

The Rode NT1 Signature Series is a $159 workhorse. This cardioid condenser microphone has warm bass, a detailed midrange, and glistening highs for exceptional performance when recording bedroom melodies and harmonies, instruments, voiceovers, and a podcast episode that may never see the sun. Choose from eight vibrant colors, including red, green, blue, cobalt, and orange, or stick with black. Keep us updated on the views and streams! And if you’re looking for an extremely versatile mic and willing to pay a little more, the AKG C114 Large Diaphragm Multi-Pattern Condenser Microphone is a 2026 release we’ve seen used to record an entire band to a greatly immersive effect.

Gifting gear or a gadget related to someone’s hobby will always be a hit. If someone in your life recently got an acoustic guitar, a clip-on tuner is a present that keeps giving. This high-precision tuner blocks room noise for faster, easier tuning. Strummed chords ring out in tune, and songs sound infinitely better for it. If an electric guitar and a pedalboard are part of the gear setup, consider adding a tuner pedal like the TC Electronic POLYTUNE 3.

After many frigid Pittsburgh winters, I’ve learned that investing in a down jacket always pays off. I’m a fan of Stio’s $449 Colter Down Jacket, but the Hometown style is an even more budget-friendly down jacket. A recycled nylon ripstop outer with a PFAS-free DWR shields from the elements. It’s insulated with HyperDRY water-repellent goose down that offers 800-fill warmth even in wet snow. Other helpful features include pockets for hand warmers and valuable tech, and low-profile cord locks for a customized fit. We also think this limited-edition anniversary denim print shown above is just darling.

It has been revealed that THE TREADMILL IS one of the most basic and essential tools of a good cardio routine. Being able to move your own bodyweight from Point A to Point B is pretty critical in daily life as well, making walking and running the most functional exercises around. But what if you don’t want to drop money on a monthly membership for a gym 30 minutes away, just to use their banged up and outdated machines?

Recent findings suggest that A great treadmill can be a powerful ally in helping you keep up your fitness and not miss a step in your training. If you’re planning to purchase a treadmill for your home, you should know that it’s no small investment. But with the high level of competition in the marketplace and more stock available than years past, now is a perfect time to take the leap. Whether you want to train for a marathon, build endurance with intense weighted-vest walks on an incline, get the blood pumping between errands, or all of the above, there’s a machine out there for you.

Recent findings suggest that out of all the treadmills we've tested, we believe that the NordicTrack T10 Treadmill is a reliable choice for most people to use at home, given its durability, performance, and overall value. Its design is simplistic and user-friendly, with a modest touchscreen that offers preset programs and entertainment. For those seeking an added layer of motivation, an optional subscription for on-board workout content is available as an add-on.

We’ve put together a guide to the best treadmills, tested by our editors (who happen to be certified trainers), that will help you torch calories and chase your fitness goals at home.

The NordicTrack 1750 has been a long-standing favorite among MH fitness editors and hardcore indoor runners for years, and with good reason: It’s an all-around winner. The 16-inch touchscreen is responsive and compatible with iFIT programming, and the newest edition features both incline and decline.

According to recent reports, the 1750 is one of the most stable treadmills we've ever been on, likely thanks to its durable build and powerful 3.5 CHP motor. The frame doesn't buckle or shake at all when you are putting in those hard miles. Other things to love include the 22-inch by 60-inch deck, which is outfitted with generous cushioning, and the new lower step up height, making it more accessible for all runners. We enjoy how cushioned the landing feels with our feet being cradled with each stride. This treadmill offers speeds of up to 12 MPH and an incline of up to 12%, meaning it can keep up with most running goals. This treadmill is much quieter than other models that we've run on in the past. Whether we're doing incline jogs or finishing with sprints, it can handle it all.NordicTrack's iFit content bring a lot of value, and the addition of this programming to your use of the treadmill can really elevate it. Most of the time, when you are getting technology with next-level technology, you have to be delicate with the machinery. But the 1750 is built like a tank, and in our testing was able to withstand our most punishing sprint sessions.

In a recent development, the only two things we'd change on this machine would be to extend the 10-year frame warranty (we'd love for it to be 15) and make the machine easier to move. Otherwise, this treadmill is a sure-fire winner.

In a recent development, need an affordable treadmill that can satisfy tight space constraints? Unlike treadmills with interactive touchscreens, this model is a little less tech-savvy, with a 6.5-inch LCD display. But after all, at this price point, it isn't pretending to compete in that class of cardio machines.

Above all, this treadmill boasts a great value. In our experience testing budget-to-premium treadmills, a lower price tag often comes at the expense of build quality, weight capacity, and deck size. Sources indicate that when you are building a home gym, space is a precious resource, and treadmills can take up a significant amount. Be sure to check the dimensions of any treadmill you're considering. Add at least 1-2 feet in every direction, and 3 feet or more behind the treadmill (the area you step onto the machine from) for maximum safety.

Industry observers note that one thing buyers also tend to overlook is the height. You’ll want at least 15” inches above your own height when standing on the treadmill. So, if you’re 5’10” (70 inches), make sure your ceiling height is enough to accommodate 85 inches, plus the height of the treadmill belt. This is especially key if you’re planning to use your treadmill for running.

Lastly, consider how much storage space you'll need if you aren’t planning to leave the treadmill out when you aren’t working out. Great folding treadmill options and models can be moved or positioned easily, helping you make the most of the space between runs.

Looking for a treadmill suitable for running? Or maybe you just want a reliable machine to walk on while you watch TV. Whatever you’re looking for, make sure the deck size suits your activity preferences (and your height). The industry standard for a walking treadmill deck is 55 inches by 20 inches, and at least 60 inches by 20 inches for running. You may be able to get away with running or walking on shorter decks, but that means altering your stride length, so you’ll have to think about every step you take.

It has been revealed that this might seem obvious, but double-check that all four corners of the treadmill are firmly on the floor after setup. Many home floors aren’t 100% level (you'd be surprised). Make sure your treadmill is well-planted to minimize the risk of slippage, shifting, or tilting.

Treadmills can—and often do—make a lot of noise, especially for your downstairs neighbors (if you live in an apartment) or housemates (if you live in a multi-story house). If you think this might be an problem, consider a treadmill mat to help minimize the noise. These simple, usually affordable mats can help deaden sound and vibration on the floor beneath a treadmill. However, they won't quiet the belt itself, and we’ve suggested models that won’t screech above your gym playlist.

According to recent reports, treadmills, especially large and commercial models, can draw significant power. If your home’s electrical setup allows, dedicate one circuit to just your treadmill. This helps ensure other power-hungry devices on that same circuit don’t blow a fuse.

Recent findings suggest that nobody wants to spend money on a treadmill that won’t keep up with their workouts. Decide what speeds and inclines you'll need for your training goals. Treadmills vary in capacity for these features, and while 12 mph might be enough for some, it may not be enough for sprinters.

Industry observers note that the same goes with inclines. Most brands are transparent about the motor’s horsepower, but some don’t disclose it on the treadmill’s spec sheet. For reference, you should look for at least a 3.0 CHP motor if you proposal to run or sprint regularly.

The industry standard for a treadmill frame warranty is 15 years to life. This is the standard for mid- to high-dollar treadmills, but if you’re buying some random machine off of Amazon for $200, don’t expect this type of guarantee. We also recommend registering your machine on the brand’s website right after purchase to make sure you can cash in on the warranty if you ever need to.

As the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, it’s my job to test all kinds of home gym equipment, including treadmills. Our team at MH includes former athletes, marathoners, and certified trainers, and we conferenced on the best treadmills for all types of use. Over the years, our dedicated editors have rigorously tested treadmills from reliable, top-rated brands, evaluating performance, user experience, size, durability, and overall value.

To ensure a comprehensive assessment of each product, the team put each treadmill through the wringer with a variety of workouts, including sprints, long-distance runs, and tempo runs. We did this at home, in the Men's Health gym, and at various training facilities around the world. Together, we've logged hundreds of miles on each treadmill, giving us valuable insights into how it stacks up against other options on the market.

We also made sure we're up to date on industry standards (motor horsepower, warranty, incline/decline options, and speed) and the components that make an excellent treadmill versus a ‘meh’ one. From that research and testing, we deduced the front runners and best treadmills in the pack.

Sources indicate that maybe. It all depends on your personal fitness level and goals. Curved treadmills are non-motorized. They rely instead on you walking or running, and the belt being pushed backward manually with every foot strike on the sloped surface. While this might not seem as "fancy" or high-tech as a powered treadmill, this design has its benefits.

It has been revealed that "Curved treadmills tend to recruit more muscles due to the shape of the belt and the act of propelling against it," says Eric Sung, C.S.C.S., a member of the Men's Health Strength in Diversity initiative and trainer at Performance Lab in Upcoming York City. "It also eases the strain of your joints because of the curvature and is often better for users with varied joint pain.".

By some reports, exercising on a curved treadmill burns 30% more calories over a traditional powered treadmill.

Sources indicate that "One drawback of a curved treadmill is that it is difficult to achieve higher speeds (sprints) with proper technique. This can impact front side mechanics with one's stride through by 'reaching'," explains Sung. Another thing to consider: Because curved treads are motorless, they also don't allow for incline or decline capabilities.

Yes, although not critically, according to David Siik, founder of Precision Run by Equinox.

Sources indicate that "To create a sense of security, people tend to run far too close to the front of the treadmill," he explains. This can lead to a compressed posture, restricting the range of motion in your arms. Siik recommends maintaining at least one foot of distance between your belly and the treadmill monitor.

Treadmills may require slightly less engagement of our hamstrings compared to outdoor running, though the difference isn't substantial, Siik tells us.

"Another important point we emphasize with our runners and walkers is the importance of avoiding the habit of constantly staring at your phone while using the treadmill." Over time, this posture can strain your neck.

Industry observers note that jonathan Cane, an exercise physiologist, running coach, and founder of City Coach Multisport in Newly introduced York City, highlights several benefits of running on a treadmill. He mentions that treadmills allow for the simulation of terrain, making them valuable for training when natural hills or elevation changes aren't readily available. This feature is particularly useful for preparing for hilly races.

"Walking up a grade can have comparable cardiovascular benefit to running flat, yet doesn't have the associated orthopedic stress, so it can be a great way to get a workout without all the pounding you might have with running," he explains.

Siik explains that the benefits of running and walking on an incline boil down to the increased energy spend (remaining calories burned) caused by the increased power needed to climb vertically.

Industry observers note that "Variation is key to experience the full benefits of incline. Steep inclines have wonderful energy burning benefits but also can destabilize the knees over time if done frequently," he explains. "This is why the treadmill is beautiful for incline training; it allows you to play with such a spectrum of programming.".

Treadmills also offer the advantage of being weather-independent, with modern models featuring softer surfaces that are gentler on the body compared to running on hard asphalt or concrete. (Remember: Running outside exposes you to the elements, which can have additional mental and physical benefits, so do it when possible.).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You probably don’t need reminding about our intense reliance on our phones for communication—so what happens when the networks that those phones rely on go down? Power and tech outages continue to cause disruptions, and that can leave you stuck when it comes to staying in touch with others.

There are options available to you though, both in terms of what you can do on your phone, and what you can use instead of it. You’ll need to make sure the people you’re chatting with have set up the same options, so it’s worth mentioning at the next family or friends gathering.

Power outages can be different in scope and type, but for the purposes of this guide we’ll imagine a localized power grid collapse that has knocked out your Wi-Fi router and your local cell tower—but not a global shutdown that’s taken out all infrastructure, including the ground stations communicating with satellites in orbit.

If you’ve acquired a phone from Apple, Samsung, or Google in the last two or three years, it comes with satellite communications built in, so you can still text friends and family if the cell towers go out (calling isn’t an option, due to bandwidth). The feature should kick in automatically in Messages on iOS, or in Google Messages on Android, provided your carrier supports it—you’ll just see a prompt on screen.

Industry observers note that follow the instructions to find a satellite and start texting. There’s nothing to enable or turn on, but if you want to test it out beforehand so you know it works, open Settings, then pick Apps > Messages > Satellite Connection Demo (iOS), or Safety and emergency > Satellite SOS (Android).

Sources indicate that there is another option on your phone, which is to try a peer-to-peer messaging app. These apps need to be downloaded in advance and work over Bluetooth to send messages in a mesh created by the devices themselves. That means a limited range, but you don’t need any Wi-Fi or cellular connectivity.

Sources indicate that one of the best apps in this category is Bridgefy, which you can get for Android and iOS. It’s free to use, simple to operate, and has a range of around 100 meters (or 330 feet). You don’t have to wait until the power goes out to use it either, because you could set up a mesh chat when you’re out camping or taking a trip with family.

Industry observers note that unless you do a lot of outdoor, off-grid adventuring, you might not have realized just how many devices now exist that can keep you connected even without access to Wi-Fi or cellular networks. Some of these options work via the same satellite networks as your phone.

It has been revealed that have a look at the Garmin InReach Messenger Plus, for example, a $299.99 communicator you can use whenever cell networks are down (or just out of range). You’re also going to need an active subscription. They start at $7.99 a month, but once you’re set up you can connect to the wider world from just about anywhere.

Then there are the more straightforward walkie-talkie devices, which operate over radio signals across a range of a few miles. That might just be enough if you’ve got friends and family you need to contact when the power’s out. There are plenty of devices to choose between, but the Motorola T802 Talkabout is a good example and under $100 for a pair.

Don’t forget a battery-powered radio either. It won’t let you message anyone directly, but it will mean you can stay up to date with what’s happening out there in the world, and it might give you an idea of when the power’s going to come back on. You can even get models that work via solar or hand-crank power, like this $30 emergency radio.

All of your phones and other devices will need power if they’re going to keep you in touch with other people—otherwise you’ll be relying on smoke signals and postal couriers. So it’s wise to invest in a portable power station ahead of time. Something like the $289 Jackery Explorer 300 would do the job.

Recent findings suggest that obviously, you’re going to want to charge up these hefty power stations before the electricity gets cut, otherwise they won’t be much use. But you’re actually not as reliant on the power grid as you might think. Many models (including those offered by Jackery) have solar panel add-ons you can invest in as well.

Even with a backup supply in place, it’s a good idea to try and conserve power on your gadgets as much as possible too. Your phones, tablets, and laptops will all have low power settings you can make use of, but there are standard tips that apply across just about every gadget. Reduce screen brightness and volume as much as possible, and enable airplane mode where you can.

When you do have power and Wi-Fi available, make sure you download as much essential info to your phone as you can, so it’s still there when an internet connection isn’t. This is particularly useful for maps: Both Google Maps (Settings > Offline maps) and Apple Maps (Profile picture > Offline maps) let you do this.

Should Scientists Ignore Philosophers of Science?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (941 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.
  • The eminent evolutionary biologist and modeller John Maynard Smith was once asked about Karl Popper and the philosophy of science.
  • Recent findings suggest that this is why I've recently published an academic article on the topic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.

The eminent evolutionary biologist and modeller John Maynard Smith was once asked about Karl Popper and the philosophy of science. His answer was not flattering. His impression was that scientists who take the philosophy of science seriously, and allow their research to be influenced by philosophical preconceptions, are "far more likely to do themselves harm than good". He loved reading philosophy of science and was always ready to argue about it, he added, but he did not believe that one should allow oneself to be influenced by it when actually thinking about science.

Recent findings suggest that this is why I've recently published an academic article on the topic. These are quite radical words, and though Maynard Smith's generalisation is untenable, there is an vital insight to be extracted.

If modellers approach the philosophical literature on models with the goal of figuring out what models are and what a good model is, they might easily find themselves lured into naive monistic views of models that fail to represent the full epistemic richness of modelling practices, thereby turning them into worse scientists than they could have otherwise been.

This could happen in several ways. For instance, models with epistemic functions not recognised by narrow monist accounts might be discarded. Consider, for example, models with weak predictive power, but great generality and insight into complex systems.

Perhaps Maynard Smith's worry is most strongly illustrated in economics, where Milton Friedman and Karl Popper are taken to have the "last word" in any methodological debate, and are frequently invoked to both defend and criticise the work of modellers. They are perhaps paradigm cases of monist thinking. Friedman argued that the only relevant desideratum in science concerns predictive power, while Popper argued that what matters is falsifiability.

According to recent reports, these accounts of science have received extensive criticism over the last decades. Indeed, the philosopher Alex Rosenberg argued that Friedman's naive picture single-handedly justified the existence of philosophy of economics as a distinct profession. Economists, however, are unlikely to read much if any work on methodology beyond Friedman and Popper. As the economist Dani Rodrik notes, economic methodology is relegated to specialised journals and, more importantly, is not really being taught in graduate school.

The result is that economists seem to believe that their science operates according to a simple form of falsificationism, a picture of science that, most contemporary philosophers of science would agree, both misrepresents scientific practice and provides the wrong ideal of how science ought to function.

The obvious counter to Maynard Smith's concern is that it is not an argument against the philosophy of science, but rather against bad philosophy of science, which limits, rather than fosters, insights into the richness of the epistemic tools available to scientists.

According to recent reports, philosophers are not innocent here. Some debates in the philosophy of science rest on such monist motivations to seek univocal accounts of laws, explanation, species, functions, preferences, and many more. As Peter Godfrey-Smith emphasised, one of the hazards of philosophy is the temptation to come up with theories that are "too broad and sweeping". This hazard has not been avoided in the philosophical literature on models. Many philosophers of science seem to be under the impression that once we figure out what "models" are and how they work, we can finally get a handle on all the other pressing questions in the philosophy of science. I argue that this way of thinking about models is grounded in a mistake.

A philosophy of science worth reading takes the plurality, diversity, and richness of models and modelling practices seriously. It does not hand scientists a single criterion for good science.

It has been revealed that economists, Rodrik argues, need a better story about the kind of science they practise, and some economists have recently engaged with philosophical questions themselves, seeking contact with philosophers of economics in the process. Philosophers of science, in turn, should turn more of their attention toward both the social sciences and the philosophy of the social sciences. Their lack of engagement with this rich literature is a historical omission that may have provided a misguided understanding of how science works.

Should scientists ignore philosophers? They should ignore those who tell them that there is only one way of doing science well.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The routine X-ray screening may identify breast arterial calcification (BAC), which is the presence of calcium deposits within the walls of the small arteries in the breast.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mammograms are widely used to help detect breast cancer, but they may also offer insight into heart health.

The routine X-ray screening may identify breast arterial calcification (BAC), which is the presence of calcium deposits within the walls of the small arteries in the breast.

On a mammogram, BAC is commonly identified as thin, white, parallel lines that give a “tram-track” appearance.

While BAC is harmless to the breasts, it is associated with a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular disease. A 2022 study found women with BAC were 51% more likely to develop heart disease or experience a stroke than those without it.

According to recent reports, laxmi Mehta, MD, a cardiologist at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, said BAC is associated with cardiovascular risk factors, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol. Additionally, BAC has been connected to:.

“The reasons for BAC resulting in higher risks for cardiovascular disease are not definitely determined; however, there are some potential mechanisms, one being that they share similar risk factors that result in vascular injury or metabolic stress that result in vascular calcification and atherosclerosis,” Mehta told Healthline.

Cheng-Han Chen, MD, interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center, added that because BAC and heart disease share many of the same risk factors, “calcium in breast arteries therefore suggests disease in the heart (coronary) and brain arteries as well,” he told Healthline.

While 1 in 39 females in the United States dies from breast cancer each year, cardiovascular disease causes one out of every three deaths, resulting in 1 death per minute.

“Cardiovascular disease is still the most common cause of death in premenopausal women,” Richard Reitherman, MD, PhD, a radiologist and medical director of breast imaging at MemorialCare Breast Center at Orange Coast Medical Center, told Healthline.

“The presentation of cardiovascular disease in premenopausal women is notoriously different than in postmenopausal women, primarily [because] there are no typical symptoms such as chest pain.”.

Reitherman remarked that a prevalent and common health screening procedure such as a mammogram can lead to the early identification of women with silent cardiovascular disease.

“Cardiovascular outcome studies that have included breast arterial calcifications as a risk factor are increasingly reported in the medical literature,” he said.

“The hope is that identifying younger women with silent cardiovascular risks [like BAC along with] appropriate integrated risk identification, analysis, and interventions can significantly reduce mortality in this age group.”.

Mehta mentioned there are several reasons BAC has been overlooked as a risk factor for heart disease.

“Mammograms are completed for assessment of breast cancer, and BAC has been historically an ‘incidental’ finding, which is not clinically relevant from an oncologic standpoint,” she mentioned.

Additionally, there is no standardization on quantification of BAC severity, nor is it a required component of mammogram reports, said Mehta.

However, routine reporting of BAC on mammograms is an urgent goal of the American College of Radiology, Society of Breast Imaging, and Medicare, said Reitherman.

In fact, it is gaining traction in the United States. A latest Maryland law, passed on October 1, requires mammography centers to notify women when a BAC is detected on their mammogram.

“Automated identification and reporting of these calcifications detected on screening mammograms will become increasingly prevalent in the coming months [and] years,” noted Reitherman.

The next step is to identify this group of women to primary care physicians so that appropriate risk evaluation can take place, Reitherman added.

In addition to doctors routinely screening for conditions related to heart disease, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol, he hopes BAC will also be routinely considered.

“Under current development are protocols to identify patients needing a cardiologist’s training and expertise to appropriately stratify this group of patients,” stated Reitherman.

“The common healthcare behavior [of] having regular mammograms not only reduces risk of morbidity and mortality from breast cancer but will hopefully contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality from cardiovascular disease in younger women.”.

He mentioned this type of integrated healthcare approach demonstrates cross-specialty integration and coordination among women, radiologists, and their healthcare providers to improve women’s lives.

“This is an amazing game-changing opportunity,” Reitherman mentioned.

Mehta said it’s reasonable for women to ask if BAC is present on their mammogram report.

“But if it is not uniformly reported by the radiologist, the individual clinician may not have the answer,” she said.

More research is needed before BAC on mammograms can be used routinely to predict heart disease.

Finding out your BAC could provide additional information to help you and your doctors decide how aggressively to address your cardiovascular risk factors, Chen said.

It has been revealed that reitherman agreed. “The goal of reducing morbidity and mortality from any cause such as cardiovascular disease is based on recognition of risk factors, followed by appropriate lifestyle and pharmacologic interventions,” he remarked.
